children.summary: Part I provides a comprehensive overview of Corning Incorporated, detailing its history, business segments, and market strategies. children.title: Overview of Corning Incorporated and Its Business Segments
children.summary: Corning Incorporated, established in 1851 and incorporated in 1936, specializes in glass science, ceramic science, and optical physics, producing innovative products that enhance various industries. The company operates in multiple sectors, including optical communications, mobile consumer electronics, and environmental technologies, with a focus on research and development. Corning manufactures at 124 plants across 15 countries and is organized into five segments: Optical Communications, Display Technologies, Specialty Materials, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences. The Optical Communications segment, a pioneer in low-loss optical fiber, addresses the growing demand for optical solutions in telecommunications and enterprise networks.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Optical Communications Segment
children.summary: The Optical Communications Segment details Corning's pioneering role in optical fiber technology since 1970, highlighting its transition from copper to optical systems in telecommunications. It categorizes products into carrier and enterprise networks, with carrier offerings including various optical fibers and cable solutions designed for high-performance applications like 5G. The segment also emphasizes the importance of hardware and equipment, such as connectors and network interface devices, in supporting integrated optical solutions. Manufacturing facilities are located globally, and the segment accounted for 34% of Corning's total net sales in 2022.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Display Technologies Segment
children.summary: This section details Corning's Display Technologies segment, highlighting its leadership in precision glass innovations for high-resolution displays. Key products include Corning® EAGLE XG® Slim Glass for thinner screens, Corning® Astra® Glass for high-resolution applications, and Corning® Lotus™ NXT Glass for flexible devices. The segment accounted for 22% of Corning's total net sales in 2022 and operates manufacturing facilities across Asia. The importance of patent protection and proprietary trade secrets is also emphasized.

children.title: Overview of Specialty Materials Segment Operations and Products
children.summary: The Specialty Materials Segment focuses on manufacturing ceramic substrates and filter products for emissions control in mobile applications. Key developments include the introduction of low-mass Corning® FLORA® substrates and Corning® DuraTrap® GC gasoline particulate filters, which address tightening global emissions regulations. The segment operates globally, with manufacturing facilities in New York, Virginia, China, and Germany, and represents 11% of Corning's total segment net sales in 2022. Patent protection is crucial for the segment's operations, with a significant portfolio of patents related to its products and technologies.

children.title: Overview of Environmental Technologies Segment
children.summary: The Environmental Technologies segment focuses on manufacturing ceramic substrates and filter products for emissions control in mobile applications globally. It highlights the development of high-performance cellular ceramic substrates since the 1970s, which are now standard in catalytic converters. The section discusses recent innovations like low-mass Corning® FLORA® substrates and Corning® DuraTrap® GC gasoline particulate filters, and outlines the global manufacturing locations. It also emphasizes the importance of patent protection for its technologies and notes that this segment accounted for 11% of Corning’s total net sales in 2022.

children.title: Overview of Life Sciences Segment and Its Offerings
children.summary: The Life Sciences Segment focuses on developing and supplying laboratory products for over 105 years, catering to researchers and drug manufacturers. It offers consumables like plastic vessels, liquid handling plastics, and cell culture media, essential for drug discovery, diagnostics, and bioproduction. The segment markets products under brands such as Corning®, Falcon®, and PYREX®, primarily to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies globally. Patent protection and brand recognition are crucial for its operations, with the segment contributing 8% to Corning's total net sales in 2022.

children.title: Overview of Hemlock and Emerging Growth Businesses
children.summary: This section discusses Corning's Hemlock and Emerging Growth Businesses, which includes pharmaceutical technologies, automotive glass solutions, and other corporate investments, accounting for 11% of total segment net sales in 2022. It outlines the competitive landscape across various segments, including Optical Communications, Display Technologies, Specialty Materials, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences, highlighting key competitors and the company's strategies for maintaining market position through innovation and customer relationships. The section emphasizes the importance of research and development, product quality, and supply reliability in sustaining competitive advantages.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Competitive Landscape and Strategies
children.summary: This section discusses Corning's competitive landscape across its various business segments, including Optical Communications, Display Technologies, Specialty Materials, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences. children.title: 2022 Financial Results Overview
children.summary: In 2022, Corning reported net sales of $14.2 billion, a 1% increase from 2021, driven by significant growth in Optical Communications and Hemlock and Emerging Growth Businesses, despite a decline in Display Technologies. Net income decreased to $1.316 billion, influenced by increased severance and legal costs, as well as adverse foreign currency impacts. Diluted earnings per share rose by 20% due to share repurchases, despite the overall decrease in net income. The section also provides a corporate outlook for Q1 2023, projecting core sales between $3.2 billion and $3.4 billion.

The section emphasizes the importance of quarterly reviews and the judgment required in determining whether impairment exists. Additionally, it discusses the sensitivity of ongoing pension and OPEB expenses to changes in key assumptions, such as spot rates and expected returns on assets, providing estimated financial impacts of these changes. The section emphasizes the importance of understanding how economic factors can influence multiple assumptions simultaneously.

children.title: Understanding Forward-Looking Statements and Risks
children.summary: This section outlines the nature of forward-looking statements in Corning's Annual Report, which include predictions about future performance, market share, revenue growth, and innovation. It emphasizes that these statements are inherently uncertain and subject to various risks, such as economic trends, competition, geopolitical issues, and supply chain disruptions. The section lists specific factors that could cause actual results to differ from expectations, including changes in market conditions, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, and regulatory developments. It clarifies that while the company believes its forward-looking statements are based on reasonable assumptions, it does not commit to updating these statements unless legally required.

children.title: Market Risks: Currency Exposure and Hedging Strategies
children.summary: This section discusses the company's exposure to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations due to its international operations, particularly focusing on currencies like the Japanese yen and euro. It outlines the use of over-the-counter derivative instruments, such as foreign exchange forward and option contracts, to mitigate risks associated with these fluctuations. The section also includes a sensitivity analysis indicating that a 10% adverse movement in exchange rates could lead to significant losses in fair value, specifically noting potential impacts related to the Japanese yen. Additionally, it emphasizes the company's strategy to offset these risks through hedging activities and the management's expectation that losses from derivatives will be counterbalanced by gains on hedged assets and liabilities.

children.title: Corning's Governance and Executive Overview
children.summary: PART III provides an overview of Corning's governance structure, detailing the backgrounds and roles of its Board of Directors and executive officers. It includes information on the Code of Ethics for executives, executive compensation and equity plans, security ownership, and related transactions. The section emphasizes the importance of director independence and the integrity of financial audits, highlighting the role of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP. Additionally, it outlines the company's commitment to ethical standards and corporate governance practices.

children.title: Directors and Executive Officers Overview
children.summary: This section provides an overview of Corning's Board of Directors and executive officers, detailing their backgrounds and roles. It includes a list of board members, highlighting their previous positions and experience in various industries, such as finance, healthcare, and technology. The section also references the Definitive Proxy Statement for additional information on corporate governance and the election of directors. Readers can learn about the qualifications and expertise of the individuals guiding Corning's strategic direction.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Executive Officers
children.summary: This section provides a detailed overview of the executive officers of Corning's Board of Directors, including their professional backgrounds, roles, and ages. Key figures include Donald W. Blair, Leslie A. Brun, Stephanie A. Burns, Richard T. Clark, Pamela J. Craig, and Robert F. Cummings, Jr., each with extensive experience in various industries such as finance, healthcare, and technology. The section highlights their previous positions and contributions to other organizations, illustrating the diverse expertise they bring to Corning's leadership. Readers can learn about the qualifications and career trajectories of these executives, which may inform assessments of the company's governance and strategic direction.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Board of Directors
children.summary: This section provides detailed profiles of the members of Corning's Board of Directors, including their professional backgrounds, roles, and ages. Key figures include Donald W. Blair, Leslie A. Brun, and Wendell P. Weeks, highlighting their previous executive positions at major companies like NIKE, Procter & Gamble, and Merck. The section emphasizes the diverse expertise and leadership experience of the board members, which spans various industries such as finance, technology, and healthcare. Readers can learn about the qualifications and contributions of each board member to Corning's governance.

children.title: Code of Ethics for Executives
children.summary: The Code of Ethics outlines the ethical standards and expectations for the Chief Executive Officer and financial executives at Corning Incorporated. It has been in place for over ten years and applies specifically to key financial leaders within the organization. The section notes that there were no amendments or waivers to the Code in 2022 and provides information on how shareholders can access the Code. Additionally, it mentions the commitment to disclose any future changes to the Code on the company's website.

children.title: Overview of Executive Compensation and Equity Plans
children.summary: This section provides an overview of executive compensation, referencing the 'Compensation Discussion and Analysis,' 'Director Compensation,' and 'Compensation and Talent Management Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation' from the Definitive Proxy Statement. It includes a table detailing the company's equity compensation plans as of December 31, 2022, showing the number of securities to be issued upon exercise of outstanding options, the weighted-average exercise price, and the number of securities available for future issuance. The total number of outstanding options is 9,664,672 with a weighted-average exercise price of $22.92, and 32,332,203 securities remain available for future issuance under approved plans.

children.title: Security Ownership and Equity Compensation Overview
children.summary: This section provides details on the security ownership of certain beneficial owners and management, specifically referencing the 'Beneficial Ownership Table' from the Definitive Proxy Statement. It includes information about the company's equity compensation plans as of December 31, 2022, detailing the number of securities to be issued upon exercise of outstanding options, warrants, and rights, along with their weighted-average exercise price. Additionally, it outlines the number of securities remaining available for future issuance under equity compensation plans, distinguishing between those approved and not approved by security holders.

children.title: Equity Compensation Plans Overview
children.summary: This section provides detailed information on the company's equity compensation plans as of December 31, 2022. It includes the number of securities to be issued upon exercise of outstanding options, warrants, and rights, which totals 9,664,672, with a weighted-average exercise price of $22.92. Additionally, it states that there are 32,332,203 securities remaining available for future issuance under equity compensation plans approved by security holders. The section distinguishes between plans approved and not approved by security holders, although only approved plans are detailed here.

children.title: Related Transactions and Director Independence Policies
children.summary: This section incorporates by reference the company's policies on transactions with related persons and director independence from the Definitive Proxy Statement. It highlights the importance of these policies in ensuring corporate governance and board integrity. Additionally, it mentions that PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (PwC) provided an independence letter to the Audit Committee, confirming their independence in relation to the audit of the financial statements. The Audit Committee has acknowledged and discussed PwC's independence, reinforcing the company's commitment to ethical standards.

children.title: Principal Accounting Fees and Services Overview
children.summary: This section discusses the fees paid to the independent registered public accounting firm, PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP (PwC), and the policy regarding the pre-approval of audit and non-audit services by the Audit Committee. It confirms PwC's independence as per the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board standards, which is essential for the integrity of the audit opinion on the financial statements. The Audit Committee has engaged in discussions with PwC regarding its independence, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements.

children.title: Exhibits and Form 10-K Summary for Corning Incorporated
children.summary: PART IV includes a comprehensive list of exhibits and agreements filed by Corning Incorporated, detailing financial statements, corporate governance documents, and historical agreements with partners like Samsung Display. It also summarizes the Form 10-K, highlighting significant agreements such as officer severance and change in control agreements, along with equity plans for non-employee directors. The section includes necessary certifications under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and concludes with signatures from executives affirming the report's accuracy and compliance.

children.title: List of Exhibits and Agreements Filed
children.summary: This section lists various exhibits filed as part of the report, including financial statements and agreements related to Corning Incorporated. Key documents include the Framework Agreement with Samsung Display, multiple transaction agreements, and amendments to the company's bylaws and pension plans. Each exhibit is referenced with its filing date and source, providing a comprehensive overview of legal and financial commitments. Readers can learn about the company's corporate governance, financial arrangements, and historical agreements with partners.

children.title: Form 10-K Summary and Signatures
children.summary: This section provides a summary of the Form 10-K, including references to various agreements and plans related to Corning Incorporated. It lists significant documents such as officer severance agreements, change in control agreements, and equity plans for non-employee directors. Additionally, it includes certifications required under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and details about the company's subsidiaries and independent auditor consent. The section concludes with signatures from key executives and directors, affirming the report's accuracy and compliance with regulatory requirements.

children.title: Independent Auditor's Report on Financial Statements and Controls
children.summary: This section contains the report from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm, regarding their audit of Corning Incorporated's consolidated financial statements and internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2022. The firm expresses an unqualified opinion that the financial statements fairly present the company's financial position and results of operations in accordance with U.S. GAAP. It details the responsibilities of both management and the auditors, the audit process, and the inherent limitations of internal controls. Additionally, it highlights a critical audit matter concerning the company's tax receivables related to South Korean tax disputes, emphasizing the significant judgment involved in management's assessment of uncertain tax positions.

children.title: Corning's Consolidated Income Statements Overview
children.summary: This section presents the Consolidated Statements of Income for Corning Incorporated for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020. It details key financial metrics including net sales, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, and net income. Readers can learn about the company's financial performance trends over the three years, including changes in operating income and net income attributable to shareholders. The section also provides earnings per share figures and reconciles net income attributable to Corning with net income available to common shareholders.

children.title: Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income Overview
children.summary: This section presents the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income for Corning Incorporated and its subsidiaries for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020. It details net income figures, which show a decrease from 2021 to 2022, and outlines components of other comprehensive income, including foreign currency translation adjustments and postretirement benefit plan costs. The section also highlights comprehensive income, including amounts attributable to non-controlling interests and Corning Incorporated itself, providing insights into the company's overall financial performance and changes in equity. Readers can learn about the factors affecting comprehensive income and the company's financial trends over the three years.

children.title: Consolidated Balance Sheets Overview
children.summary: This section presents the consolidated balance sheets for Corning Incorporated as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. It details the company's assets, including current assets like cash, receivables, and inventories, as well as long-term assets such as property and goodwill. The liabilities section outlines current and long-term obligations, including debt and accrued liabilities. Additionally, it provides a breakdown of shareholders' equity, including common stock, retained earnings, and treasury stock. The total assets equal total liabilities and equity, ensuring the balance sheet is balanced.

children.title: Consolidated Cash Flow Statements Overview
children.summary: This section presents the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for Corning Incorporated for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020. It details cash flows from operating, investing, and financing activities, highlighting net income, adjustments, and changes in assets and liabilities. Key figures include net cash provided by operating activities, cash used in investing activities, and cash used in financing activities. The section also shows the effect of exchange rates on cash and the cash and cash equivalents at the beginning and end of each year.

children.title: Significant Accounting Policies Overview
children.summary: This section provides an overview of Corning Incorporated's significant accounting policies, including the organization and principles of consolidation for its financial statements. It details the inclusion of subsidiaries and the elimination of intercompany transactions. The section also addresses the accounting treatment for investments in partially-owned affiliates and variable interest entities (VIEs). Furthermore, it emphasizes the use of estimates in financial reporting, particularly in areas such as revenue recognition, asset impairment, and tax liabilities, which can impact future financial results.

children.title: Significant Accounting Policies Overview
children.summary: This section outlines the significant accounting policies of Corning Incorporated, detailing the organization, basis of presentation, and principles of consolidation. It explains that the consolidated financial statements include Corning and its subsidiaries, with intercompany transactions eliminated. The section also discusses the accounting for investments in partially-owned affiliates and variable interest entities (VIEs). Additionally, it highlights the use of estimates in financial statement preparation, emphasizing areas such as revenue recognition, asset impairment, and tax liabilities, which may affect future reported results.

children.title: Summary of Corning's Significant Accounting Policies
children.summary: This section outlines Corning's significant accounting policies, covering contract assets and liabilities, research and development costs, foreign currency remeasurement, share-based compensation, stock options, cash equivalents, and allowances for doubtful accounts. It also details the accounting treatment for inventories, property, plant, and equipment, leasing practices, long-lived asset impairment, goodwill testing, government assistance, environmental liabilities, equity method investments, employee retirement plans, income tax accounting, and fair value measurements. Each subsection provides insights into how these financial elements are managed and reported, emphasizing their implications on the company's financial performance and compliance with accounting standards.

children.title: Overview of Contract Assets and Liabilities
children.summary: This section discusses contract assets and liabilities in Corning's revenue recognition process. It explains that contract assets, such as costs to obtain or fulfill contracts, are minor, with most fulfillment costs classified as inventory or fixed assets. Contract liabilities include customer deposits and deferred revenue, primarily related to Display products and HSG, respectively. The section highlights that other advanced payments are not significant and are recorded as accrued liabilities. Overall, it provides insight into how Corning manages and reports its contractual financial obligations.

children.title: Overview of Research and Development Costs
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment of research and development (R&D) costs, which are expensed as incurred. It provides specific figures for R&D expenditures over the past three years, totaling $0.9 billion in 2022, $0.8 billion in 2021, and $1.0 billion in 2020. The section emphasizes the immediate recognition of these costs in financial statements, highlighting their impact on the company's financial performance. Readers can learn about the company's commitment to R&D and its financial implications.

children.title: Foreign Currency Functional Currency and Remeasurement Gains
children.summary: This section discusses the determination of functional currency for Corning's foreign subsidiaries, primarily identifying local currencies as functional currencies, with a notable exception for a Taiwanese subsidiary using Japanese yen. It explains how foreign currency transactions are remeasured, with gains and losses recognized in income based on exchange rate fluctuations. The section provides specific figures for net foreign currency remeasurement gains and losses for the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021, and 2020, highlighting a gain of $130 million in 2022.

children.title: Overview of Share-Based Compensation Accounting
children.summary: This section covers the accounting treatment for share-based compensation, specifically focusing on time-based restricted stock and performance-based restricted stock units (PSUs). It explains that time-based awards are discretionary, vest in common stock, and have their fair value determined by the stock's market price at grant. For non-employee Board members, compensation expense is recognized immediately. In contrast, PSUs are contingent on achieving performance targets, vest over three years, and their fair value is also based on the grant date stock price, with considerations for forfeiture rates in expense recognition.

children.title: Time-Based Restricted Stock and Units Overview
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment for time-based restricted stock and restricted stock units issued by the Company. It explains that these awards are discretionary and payable in common stock upon vesting, with their fair value determined by the stock's closing market price on the grant date. For non-employee Board members, compensation expense is recognized immediately due to the absence of vesting terms. Additionally, it contrasts these with performance-based restricted stock units, which require target achievement for vesting.

children.title: Performance-Based Restricted Stock Units Overview
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment and valuation of performance-based restricted stock units (PSUs) granted by Corning. PSUs are awarded based on the achievement of specific performance targets and are payable in shares of common stock upon vesting, typically over a three-year period. The fair value of these awards is determined using the closing market price of the stock on the grant date, assuming target performance levels will be met. Additionally, it outlines the recognition of compensation expense and the impact of forfeiture rates on the accounting for these awards.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Stock Options and Valuation
children.summary: This section details Corning's stock option plans, which include non-qualified and incentive stock options that allow employees to purchase shares at the market price on the grant date. Options typically vest over one to five years and have a maximum term of ten years. The fair value of these options is estimated using a multiple-point Black-Scholes model, incorporating factors such as volatility, dividend yield, and risk-free rates. The section also explains how the expected term of options is calculated based on historical exercise experience and current vesting periods.

children.title: Overview of Cash and Cash Equivalents
children.summary: This section defines cash equivalents as highly liquid investments that can be quickly converted to cash, specifically those with contractual maturities of three months or less. It emphasizes that the carrying amount of these securities approximates their fair value due to their short-term nature. Additionally, it provides supplemental cash flow information for the years 2020 to 2022, detailing non-cash transactions, cash paid for interest, and income taxes, including capitalized interest costs related to property, plant, and equipment.

children.title: Allowance for Doubtful Accounts in Trade Receivables
children.summary: This section discusses the allowance for doubtful accounts related to trade accounts receivable, emphasizing the estimation of probable lifetime credit losses. It explains how the allowance is determined based on historical write-off experiences and expected future default rates by industry. Additionally, it mentions the establishment of specific allowances for customers known to have financial difficulties. The section also notes that the company does not have significant off-balance-sheet credit exposure related to its customers.

children.title: Accounting Treatment of Inventories and Related Assets
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment of inventories, stating that they are recorded at the lower of cost or net realizable value using the first-in, first-out (FIFO) method. It also briefly outlines the valuation of stock options, cash equivalents, and trade accounts receivable, providing insights into how these financial elements are managed and reported. Readers can learn about the methodologies used for estimating fair values and allowances, as well as the implications of these practices on financial statements.

children.title: Accounting for Property, Plant, and Equipment
children.summary: This section details the accounting treatment for property, plant, and equipment (PP&E) at Corning. It explains that land, buildings, and equipment are recorded at cost and depreciated using the straight-line method over their estimated useful lives, which range from 10 to 40 years for buildings and 2 to 20 years for equipment. Additionally, it mentions that interest on borrowings is capitalized during construction and amortized over the asset's useful life. The section provides insight into how Corning values its physical assets and the impact of depreciation on financial statements.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Leasing Practices and Accounting
children.summary: This section details Corning's leasing practices, including the classification of leases as operating or finance leases. It explains the recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at the commencement date based on the present value of lease payments. The company uses its incremental borrowing rate or the implicit rate for this calculation and includes renewal and termination options when reasonably certain. Lease expenses for operating leases are recognized on a straight-line basis, while finance leases involve interest expense and amortization calculated using effective interest and straight-line methods.

children.title: Assessment of Long-Lived Asset Impairment
children.summary: This section outlines the process for assessing the impairment of long-lived assets, including property, plant, equipment, and intangible assets. It details the criteria for determining recoverability, which involves comparing estimated undiscounted future cash flows to the carrying value of the asset. If impairment is indicated, the fair value is calculated using an income approach based on expected future net cash flows. The section also mentions that Corning reviews impairment indicators quarterly and provides an example of a past impairment related to research and development programs.

children.title: Understanding Goodwill and Impairment Testing
children.summary: This section defines goodwill as the excess cost of an acquired entity over the assigned values of its assets and liabilities. It explains that goodwill is linked to specific reporting units and is subject to impairment testing, which occurs quarterly or when certain events arise. A detailed quantitative impairment test is conducted every three years, utilizing a discounted cash flow model to assess fair value against carrying value. The most recent test in 2020 indicated that the fair value of reporting units significantly exceeded their carrying values.

children.title: Overview of Government Assistance and Cash Incentives
children.summary: This section discusses the government assistance received by the Company, primarily in the form of cash incentives for capital expansion projects. It explains how these cash incentives are classified as liabilities and recognized when compliance with contractual conditions is probable. The section notes that cash incentives related to property, plant, and equipment are deducted from asset costs, while those related to project costs are recognized as deductions in income statements. As of December 31, 2022, the Company had significant amounts classified within liabilities for cash incentives, mainly tied to Display Technologies and Pharmaceutical Technologies.

children.title: Accrual of Environmental Liabilities and Costs
children.summary: This section outlines the Company's approach to accruing environmental liabilities, which includes costs for investigation, remediation, and maintenance when a liability is probable and estimable. It details how costs are evaluated based on site-specific facts, laws, and past experiences, and how the Company accounts for its share of costs when multiple parties are involved. Additionally, it explains the accrual process for potential liabilities that may be reimbursable by insurance, emphasizing the uncertainty in remediation outcomes and the potential for future cost adjustments.

children.title: Accounting for Equity Method Investments and Impairment
children.summary: This section discusses the accounting treatment of equity method investments, focusing on impairment reviews conducted periodically or when specific events occur. It outlines the process for assessing impairment, including measuring fair value through discounted cash flows or other methods. Additionally, it explains how equity investments not consolidated or under the equity method are measured at fair value, with changes reflected in net income. The section also mentions the measurement alternative for investments without readily determinable fair values, emphasizing that these investments were not material as of December 31, 2022, and 2021.

children.title: Overview of Employee Retirement Plans and Costs
children.summary: Corning provides defined benefit pension plans and postretirement plans, including health care and life insurance benefits for eligible retirees. The costs associated with these plans are influenced by economic conditions, demographic assumptions, and actuarial changes. Defined benefit pension costs include ongoing quarterly costs and annual mark-to-market adjustments for gains and losses. Postretirement costs also involve quarterly recognition of service and interest costs, with actuarial gains and losses amortized over employees' remaining service periods. This section outlines the financial implications and accounting methods related to these employee retirement benefits.

children.title: Income Tax Accounting and Policies
children.summary: This section details Corning's approach to accounting for income taxes using the asset and liability method, which involves recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities based on future tax consequences and differences between carrying amounts and tax bases. It explains the establishment of valuation allowances when deferred tax assets may not be realized and the assessment of the effective tax rate based on tax audits. The section also covers the recording of tax benefits for uncertain tax positions and adjustments for unrecognized tax benefits, including penalties and interest. Additionally, it discusses the indefinite reinvestment of foreign earnings under specific conditions.

children.title: Fair Value Measurements and Derivative Instruments
children.summary: This section discusses the measurement of financial assets and liabilities at fair value, both on a recurring and nonrecurring basis. It defines fair value as the price received in an orderly transaction and outlines the three-level valuation hierarchy based on observable and unobservable inputs. The section also details the use of derivative instruments for managing foreign exchange exposure, including how changes in their fair value are recorded in financial statements. Additionally, it mentions the impact of new accounting standards, specifically ASU 2021-10, on disclosure requirements regarding government assistance.

children.title: Overview of Derivative Instruments and Fair Value Accounting
children.summary: This section discusses the use of derivative instruments by the Company, specifically foreign exchange forward and option contracts, to manage foreign exchange rate fluctuations. It details how these derivatives are recorded at fair value on the balance sheet, with specific accounting treatments for cash flow hedges and fair value hedges. The section also explains the impact of changes in fair value on the consolidated statements of income, including reclassification from accumulated other comprehensive loss. Additionally, it mentions the adoption of new accounting standards related to government assistance disclosures.

children.title: HSG's Acquisition and Consolidation with Corning
children.summary: In 2020, HSG underwent significant transactions with DuPont, leading to its consolidation into Corning. HSG acquired DuPont's TCS manufacturing assets for $255 million and settled a pre-existing TCS relationship for $175 million, resulting in a pre-tax loss of $81 million for Corning. Additionally, Corning redeemed DuPont's ownership of HSG for $250 million, gaining a 100% interest in HS LLC and an 80.5% interest in HSO LLC. This transaction resulted in a pre-tax gain of $498 million for Corning, calculated based on the fair value of its equity interest in HSG. HSG's financial results have since been included in Corning's consolidated statements, although they are not material to the overall financials.

children.title: Revenue Breakdown and Recognition Details
children.summary: This section provides a detailed breakdown of Corning's revenue by major product categories for the years 2020 to 2022, highlighting trends in Telecommunication, Display, Specialty Glass, Environmental Substrate, Life Science, and Polycrystalline Silicon products. It explains the revenue recognition process, noting that most revenues are recognized when control transfers to the customer, with specific mention of customer deposits and deferred revenue related to long-term supply agreements. The section also indicates that no single customer accounted for 10% or more of total sales during the reported years, emphasizing the company's diverse customer base.

children.title: Inventory Breakdown for 2022 and 2021
children.summary: This section provides a detailed breakdown of inventories as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021, highlighting categories such as finished goods, work in process, raw materials, and supplies. The total inventory value increased from $2,481 million in 2021 to $2,904 million in 2022. Readers can learn about the specific changes in inventory categories, which reflect the company's production and supply chain dynamics over the year.

children.title: Overview of Lease Costs and Liabilities
children.summary: This section details the components of lease costs for the years 2020 to 2022, including operating, variable, and short-term lease costs, totaling $200 million in both 2022 and 2021. It also outlines cash paid for lease liabilities, with operating cash outflows from leases amounting to $116 million in 2022. The section provides supplemental balance sheet information, showing operating lease right-of-use assets and liabilities, along with the weighted-average remaining lease term and discount rate. Additionally, it lists the maturities of operating lease liabilities, totaling $1,244 million, and notes future operating leases of approximately $168 million set to commence in 2023.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Income Tax Strategies and Liabilities
children.summary: This section details Corning's income tax reconciliation, showing the effective tax rate compared to the statutory U.S. federal income tax rate for 2020-2022. It includes information on deferred tax assets and liabilities, highlighting significant temporary differences and carryforwards. The section also discusses unrecognized tax benefits, including changes due to audits and tax positions, and outlines the company's tax filing practices across various jurisdictions. Readers can learn about the company's tax strategies, potential liabilities, and the impact of foreign earnings on tax calculations.

children.title: Property, Plant and Equipment Valuation Summary
children.summary: This section details the composition and valuation of property, plant, and equipment (PP&E) net of accumulated depreciation for the years ending December 31, 2022, and 2021. It includes specific figures for land, buildings, equipment, and construction in progress, totaling $29.5 billion in 2022. The section also notes accumulated depreciation of approximately $14.1 billion, resulting in a net PP&E value of $15.4 billion. Additionally, it highlights the carrying value of precious metals in manufacturing equipment and capitalized interest costs associated with PP&E over the past three years.

children.title: Goodwill Changes and Impairment Losses Overview
children.summary: This section details the changes in the carrying amount of goodwill for Corning's business segments from December 31, 2020, to December 31, 2022. It includes specific figures for each segment, such as Optical Communications and Life Sciences, and notes the impact of foreign currency translation adjustments. The section also highlights the total gross goodwill balance and accumulated impairment losses, emphasizing the significant impairments in the Optical Communications segment. Readers can learn about the financial health and valuation adjustments of Corning's intangible assets over the specified period.

children.title: Overview of Other Assets and Liabilities
children.summary: This section details the composition of other assets and liabilities as of December 31 for the years 2022 and 2021. It includes current and non-current assets such as derivative instruments, tax deposits, operating leases, and investments, totaling $2,179 million in 2022. On the liabilities side, it outlines current and non-current obligations including wages, income taxes, and pension plan liabilities, amounting to $4,955 million in 2022. The section provides insights into the company's financial position and changes in asset and liability categories over the year.

children.title: Overview of Employee Retirement Plans and Funding Status
children.summary: This section details Corning's employee retirement plans, including defined benefit and postretirement plans. It outlines the company's contributions, funding status, and actuarial gains or losses associated with these plans. Key figures include planned contributions of $49 million for international pension plans in 2023 and a significant actuarial gain of $1.1 billion in 2022 due to increased bond yields. The section also discusses the investment strategy for plan assets, including target allocations for equities and bonds, and highlights the expected benefit payments for domestic and international pension plans and postretirement benefits.

children.title: Commitments, Contingencies, and Guarantees Overview
children.summary: This section discusses the Company's commitments, contingencies, and guarantees, detailing the recognition of liabilities for guarantees issued, which are primarily limited to financial guarantees like letters of credit and performance bonds. It outlines purchase commitments for raw materials and energy, with specified amounts due in various time frames. Additionally, it addresses ongoing litigation and environmental claims, including Corning's potential indemnification obligations related to Dow Corning and environmental cleanup liabilities, with accrued reserves for these liabilities as of December 31, 2022.

children.title: Corning's Foreign Currency Hedging Activities
children.summary: This section discusses Corning's hedging activities to manage foreign currency risks, particularly related to the Japanese yen, South Korean won, new Taiwan dollar, Chinese yuan, euro, and British pound. It details the use of over-the-counter derivative instruments, such as foreign exchange forward and option contracts, to mitigate the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on earnings. The section also outlines the company's designated cash flow hedges, including their notional values and expected gains, as well as the use of fair value hedges for leased precious metals. Additionally, it describes the assessment methods for hedge effectiveness and the use of undesignated hedges to offset economic currency risks.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Hedging Activities and Derivatives
children.summary: This section details Corning's hedging activities, focusing on the gross notional value of translated earnings contracts for 2022 and 2021. It provides data on average rate forward and option contracts in various foreign currencies, noting significant changes in notional values. The section also distinguishes between hedging and non-hedging derivative financial instruments, outlining their fair values and their effects on the company's balance sheet and earnings, including asset and liability positions.

children.title: Summary of Hedging Activities and Derivative Financial Instruments
children.summary: This section provides a detailed summary of Corning's hedging activities, specifically focusing on the total gross notional value of translated earnings contracts for the years ending December 31, 2022, and 2021. It includes data on average rate forward contracts and option contracts denominated in various foreign currencies, highlighting significant changes in notional values. Additionally, it outlines the fair values of derivative financial instruments, distinguishing between those designated as hedging instruments and those not. The section emphasizes the impact of these derivatives on the company's balance sheet and earnings, detailing asset and liability positions.

children.title: Corning's Hedging Activities and Derivative Instruments Overview
children.summary: This section details Corning's hedging activities and the impact of derivative financial instruments on its consolidated income statements from 2020 to 2022. It includes tables showing gains and losses in other comprehensive income (OCI) and their reclassification into income, with a focus on cash flow and fair value hedges. The section also reports accumulated derivative gains in other comprehensive loss as of December 31 for 2022 and 2021, and discusses the effects of de-designation of cash flow hedges, providing insights into the financial implications of Corning's hedging strategies.

children.title: Summary of Corning's Hedging Activities and Derivative Instruments
children.summary: This section provides a detailed summary of Corning's hedging activities, specifically focusing on the effects of derivative financial instruments on consolidated statements of income for the years 2020 to 2022. It includes tables that outline gains and losses recognized in other comprehensive income (OCI) and their reclassification into income, highlighting amounts related to cash flow and fair value hedges. The section also notes the accumulated derivative gains in other comprehensive loss as of December 31 for 2022 and 2021, and discusses the impact of de-designation of cash flow hedges. It details the process for submitting claims, including the requirement for written submissions and the timeline for decisions, which is generally 90 days but can be extended. If a claim is denied, the Committee must provide a written explanation, references to relevant Plan provisions, and information on how to appeal the decision. Claimants have 60 days to appeal and can submit additional information. The Committee aims to resolve appeals within 60 days, with provisions for extensions if necessary.

children.title: Claims Procedures for Employee Benefits
children.summary: This section outlines the procedures for employees or their beneficiaries to claim benefits under the Plan. It details the process for submitting claims, including the timeline for decisions and potential extensions. If a claim is denied, the Committee must provide a written explanation and information on how to appeal the decision. The appeal process is also described, including deadlines and the claimant's rights to access relevant documents. Overall, this section ensures transparency and provides a structured approach for claims and appeals.

children.title: Claims Procedures for Employee Benefits
children.summary: This section outlines the procedures for employees or their beneficiaries to claim benefits under the Plan. Claims must be submitted in writing to the Committee, which will notify the claimant of its decision within 90 days, with a possible extension of an additional 90 days if necessary. If a claim is denied, the Committee must provide a written explanation, including references to relevant Plan provisions and details on the appeals process. Claimants have 60 days to appeal a denial, can submit additional information, and will receive a decision on the appeal within 60 days, with a potential extension of up to 120 days if required.

children.title: Amendment and Termination Procedures for Claims
children.summary: This section details the procedures claimants must follow before pursuing legal action regarding benefit claims, including the requirement to exhaust all claims procedures and the applicable time limits for such actions. It also outlines the Company's rights to amend or terminate the Plan, ensuring that accrued benefits are honored if the Company is financially capable. Additionally, it specifies the delegation of authority for making technical amendments to a Vice President.

children.title: Claim Procedures and Plan Amendment Rights
children.summary: This section outlines the procedures a claimant must follow before initiating legal action regarding benefit claims, emphasizing the requirement to exhaust all claims procedures first. It specifies the time limits for bringing such actions, which are either dictated by the statute of limitations or one year from the Committee's appeal decision. Additionally, it discusses the Company's right to amend or terminate the Plan while ensuring that accrued benefits prior to any changes are honored, provided the Company is financially capable. The section also mentions the delegation of authority for technical amendments to a Vice President.

children.title: Miscellaneous Provisions of the Plan
children.summary: ARTICLE SEVEN Miscellaneous covers various aspects of the Plan, including the clarification that it does not create an employment contract, the non-transferability of benefits except under Domestic Relations Orders, and the conditions for allocating benefits through such orders. It specifies that the Plan is governed by New York law and must comply with Section 409A, detailing the tax implications for benefits and the binding nature of the Plan on successors. Additionally, it outlines the effective dates of the Plan, providing historical context and formal adoption details.

children.title: Clarification of Employment Relationship Status
children.summary: This section clarifies that the document does not establish an employment contract between the parties. It emphasizes that the terms outlined do not create any legal obligations or rights typically associated with an employment relationship. Readers can learn about the implications of this lack of a contract, including the absence of guarantees regarding employment duration or benefits. Additionally, it may address the legal context in which these terms operate, ensuring clarity on the nature of the relationship between the employee and the organization.

children.title: Non-Transferability of Benefits and Domestic Relations Orders
children.summary: This section outlines the non-transferability of benefits under the Plan, specifying that benefits cannot be assigned or transferred except under a Domestic Relations Order. It defines a Domestic Relations Order as a legal document related to child support, alimony, or marital property rights, which must meet specific criteria set by the Board. The Board has the authority to determine the validity of such orders based on applicable laws and regulations. This ensures that benefits are protected from unauthorized claims while allowing for legal obligations to be met in domestic situations.

children.title: Domestic Relations Orders and Employee Benefits Allocation
children.summary: This section outlines the conditions under which an Employee's benefits can be allocated to another individual through a Domestic Relations Order (DRO). A DRO must be issued under state law and relate to child support, alimony, or marital property rights. It establishes the rights of an Alternate Payee, such as a spouse or child, to receive benefits without accelerating payment. The Board is responsible for determining the validity of a DRO based on specific legal criteria and guidelines.

children.title: Governing Law of the Plan
children.summary: This section specifies that the Plan will be interpreted and enforced according to the laws of the State of New York. It establishes the legal framework within which the Plan operates, ensuring compliance with state law. Readers can learn about the jurisdictional authority governing the Plan and its implications for enforcement and interpretation.

children.title: Governance and Compliance with Section 409A
children.summary: Section 7.5 outlines the governance of the Plan under Section 409A, emphasizing compliance with its requirements. It states that any conflicting provisions will be amended to align with Section 409A's intent. The Committee is granted the authority to take necessary actions to ensure compliance and may utilize transition rules as needed. Additionally, it specifies that amendments made in 2007 regarding payment timing and form apply only to amounts not payable in that year.

children.title: Taxation of Plan Benefits
children.summary: This section outlines the taxation implications for benefits payable under the Plan, stating that they are subject to all applicable federal, state, and local income and employment taxes. Readers can learn about the tax obligations associated with receiving benefits from the Plan, ensuring they understand the financial responsibilities that come with these benefits.

children.title: Binding Nature of Plan on Successors
children.summary: This section states that the Plan is binding on the successors and assigns of the Company, ensuring that any future entities that take over the Company will adhere to the terms of the Plan. It emphasizes the continuity of obligations and rights under the Plan, regardless of changes in company ownership or structure. Readers can learn about the implications of corporate succession on employee benefits and the legal enforceability of the Plan in such scenarios.

children.title: Effective Dates of the Plan Document
children.summary: This section outlines the effective dates of the plan, stating that the original effective date was January 1, 1994, and the effective date of the second restated plan document is January 1, 2023. It also includes the signature of John P. MacMahon, the Senior Vice President of Global Compensation and Benefits, confirming the execution of the plan document on December 8, 2022. Readers can learn about the historical context and the formal adoption of the updated plan.
